name: large-scope-decomposition-profile
purpose: Defines how agents should handle work that is too broad, has too many files, or would exceed useful context before planning, coding, or parallel execution.

reader_guide.summary: Open this file when a request says to review everything, improve all structure, handle many files, or solve a problem whose source scope is too large for direct reading. It turns broad work into bounded slices, representative sampling, safe parallel lanes, and merge gates.
how_to_read: Read trigger_conditions to decide whether the large-scope gate applies.
Read decomposition_stages in order; do not jump directly to implementation.
Use source_inventory_rules and exclusion_rules before opening many files.
Use slice_design_rules to create bounded work units with touch paths and verification.
Use handoff_rules before calling the parallel-work-planner-agent or coding-research-agent.
Run the validation commands after changing this profile or agent spec.
update_triggers: Large tasks repeatedly consume too much context.
Agents try to read or summarize too many files at once.
A project grows enough that repository maps, dependency graphs, or source indexes become mandatory before implementation.
Parallel work planning needs a pre-step that decides slices before lanes.
A new source indexing, code search, dependency graph, or context packing tool becomes available.

structure_rules.rule: Run this large-scope gate before parallel-work-planner-agent when the task is broad, file-heavy, or context-heavy.
structure_rules.reason: Parallel lanes are useful only after the scope has been bounded into slices with clear touch paths and merge criteria.

structure_rules.rule: Create a source inventory and exclusion list before opening many files.
structure_rules.reason: Reading every file wastes context and can make the agent miss the actual ownership boundary.

structure_rules.rule: Use representative sampling for understanding, but verify final changes through targeted tests, affected checks, or global smoke checks.
structure_rules.reason: A sample is a guide, not proof that every affected path is correct.

structure_rules.rule: Every slice must define slice_id, owner, scope, touch_paths, representative_files, dependencies, output_targets, verification, and merge notes.
structure_rules.reason: Large work stays manageable only when each piece can be inspected and handed off independently.

structure_rules.rule: Record context pressure, files skipped, summaries created, and archive targets when context risk is material.
structure_rules.reason: Future agents should know why not every file was read and where the compressed context lives.

field_guide.meaning: Signals that a request is too broad or file-heavy for direct execution.
Ordered stages for shrinking the problem before implementation.
How to count and classify files without reading everything.
Folders and file types that should be skipped unless explicitly relevant.
How to split a broad task into bounded source or work slices.
The structured packet a large-scope decomposer must produce.

signals: inventory shows more than 50 candidate files
candidate files span more than 3 root projects
candidate files include generated snapshots or build outputs
the agent would need to paste or read many long files
the active conversation or file context is near saturation
understanding depends on many scattered documents
a shared config, workflow, or generated map may fan out to many outputs

source_inventory_rules: Use rg --files, repository maps, project registry, generated snapshots, dependency tools, or code search before opening broad file sets.
Group candidates by project, module, file type, owner, generated status, and risk.
Prefer entrypoints, tests, configs, schemas, public APIs, README/spec files, and recently changed files for first-pass reading.
Record counts and selection rationale instead of pasting long file lists into prompts.

exclusion_rules.exception: include only package metadata or exact dependency source when explicitly needed
include only when debugging generated Next.js output
inspect summaries or schema shape when generated output is the user-facing artifact
inspect when dependency or installation work changes lockfiles

slice_design_rules: Slice by project boundary before slicing by file type.
Slice by user-visible workflow or public API when possible.
Slice by ownership and touch_paths when parallel work may follow.
Keep generated artifacts as downstream outputs, not primary reasoning sources.
Prefer one reversible, reviewable change unit over a sweeping multi-module edit unless the requirement explicitly demands a global migration.
If multiple slices are equally valid and the trade-off is strategic or preference-based, create a human arbitration packet.

handoff_rules.to_parallel_work_planner: Use only after slices have non-overlapping touch_paths or explicit dependencies, merge gates, and verification steps.
handoff_rules.to_coding_research_agent: Use when a slice includes source-code implementation, API/library choices, architecture, performance, security, migration, or tests.
handoff_rules.to_context_archive: Use when the slice plan, file inventory, or evidence set is too large to keep in active chat.
handoff_rules.to_omission_guard: Use before close-out to verify every requested large-scope concern was either covered, deferred, or marked not applicable.

verification_rules: Run targeted checks per slice when available.
Run an affected-project check when the repository has a project graph or equivalent.
Run a global smoke check after merging slices that touch shared configs, maps, generated snapshots, or public docs.
Use omission and grounding checks for governance or research-heavy large-scope work.
